# How to Compare Two Job Offers Side by Side Using AI Safely

> **In short:** You can use any AI assistant — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Le Chat or DeepSeek — to build a side-by-side comparison of two job offers, as long as you scrub personal info first. The AI builds the table; you keep control of your privacy.

Two job offers can look almost identical on paper until you line them up next to each other. This guide shows you how to ask any AI assistant to build a comparison table from the offer details you already have, and how to keep sensitive information out of the chat. It is for anyone weighing two offers and feeling a little lost in the numbers.

## Before you start

- A free account with at least one AI assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Le Chat, DeepSeek — any one works).
- Both job offers in some written form: letters, emails, or your own notes from a phone call.
- About 15 minutes of quiet time, plus a blank note on your phone or computer where you will rewrite the offer facts by hand.

## Step 1 — Rewrite the offer facts by hand, in your own notes

Open a fresh blank note on your phone or computer — the Notes app, Google Docs, Notion, or even paper — and copy the facts of each offer into it by hand. Type out only what would go on a comparison table: job title, base pay, bonus structure, location, working hours, vacation days, health benefits, start date. Leave out your name, home address, employee ID, references, signatures, and any greeting lines.

What you see: a plain page filling with short, neutral lines. What happens next: you now have an anonymized (stripped of any detail that could identify you) summary of each offer — clean enough to share, but stripped of identifying details.

If it looks different: any plain text editor works, even your phone's notes app. The point is a fresh page, not your offer email.

💬 Example: Offer A — "Title: Senior Marketer; Base: $X; Bonus: up to 10%; Location: 3 days office, 2 remote; Vacation: 18 days; Health: full coverage; Start: 2 weeks." Use the same shape for Offer B.

You'll know it worked when a stranger could read your note and not learn your name, your address, or anything beyond the jobs themselves.

## Step 2 — Read your note once and remove anything sensitive

Before opening any AI assistant, read your note with fresh eyes and ask: is there anything here that could identify me, or that I would not want sitting on a third-party server (a company computer that stores your chat so the AI can process it)? Remove anything that answers yes.

What you see: a short checklist of risky items. What happens next: you strip your note down to the safest possible version before a single character is sent to the AI.

If it looks different: even assistants with strong privacy settings benefit from this habit. Building the muscle now means you will not accidentally share something sensitive the next time you paste text into a chat.

💬 Example: never paste your full name plus employer combo, home address, phone number, government ID numbers (Social Security, passport), bank details, names of current coworkers or your manager, references' contact info, NDA-protected clauses from your current employer, or your past salary history.

You'll know it worked when the only information left in your note is the kind you would feel comfortable writing on a public whiteboard.

## Step 3 — Open the AI assistant and paste a clear prompt

Open the assistant of your choice in a fresh chat — never inside an existing conversation, because older messages could leak in. Paste your cleaned-up note, then ask the AI to build a side-by-side comparison table.

What you see: a chat box, usually empty or with a short greeting. What happens next: the assistant returns a formatted table with one column per offer and one row per category — pay, benefits, time off, and so on.

If it looks different: every assistant has its own layout. Look for a text box labeled something like "Message", "Ask anything" or "Send a message" — yours may use slightly different words, but the idea is the same: a blank area where you type or paste.

💬 Example: "Here are the facts of two job offers I'm comparing. Please build a clear side-by-side table with one column per offer and rows for: base salary, bonus, vacation, health benefits, location, working hours, and start date. At the bottom, add a short Pros and Cons summary for each." Then paste your note.

You'll know it worked when a structured table appears on screen with both offers in their own columns and the categories you asked for in the rows.

## Step 4 — Add the things the AI cannot measure for you

The AI's table is great for numbers, but it cannot feel your gut, meet your future manager, or drive the commute at 5 p.m. Open your note again and add three rows the AI cannot fill: how the role feels, how the team treated you, and how daily life would actually work.

What you see: your note grows by a few lines. What happens next: you now have the AI's clean data side-by-side with your lived sense of each offer — the part no chatbot can replace.

If it looks different: if you only have written offers and never visited either workplace, write what you do know. Reading company reviews, looking at the office on a map, or checking the commute at peak hour all count as "your sense" of the offer.

💬 Example: add three rows — "Team vibe — Offer A felt warm in the interview; Offer B felt formal"; "Commute — Offer A 25 min by train; Offer B 55 min by car at peak"; "Growth — Offer A clearer path to senior; Offer B broader role but less clear ladder".

You'll know it worked when your final comparison has both the hard numbers from the AI and the human notes only you can write.

## Step 5 — Decide your next move and keep your privacy

Read the full table and ask which offer you keep coming back to. Then close the chat: most assistants let you delete a conversation from the side panel.

What you see: a delete or "remove" option in the chat menu. What happens next: the conversation is gone from your account; your offer details live only in your notes app, where you control them.

If it looks different: some assistants keep a short-term copy after deletion, and paid plans may save chat history by default. Look under Privacy or Data controls for a toggle like "Save conversations" or "Improve the model" — turning it off stops future chats being used to train the AI.

💬 Example: in your assistant's settings, search for a toggle named something like "Save conversations" or "Improve the model for everyone" — switch it off if you want your offer details to stay private.

You'll know it worked when you have a clear favorite between the two offers, your note is the only place the details live, and the chat is either deleted or set to stay private.

## Common mistakes

- **Pasting the whole email without cleaning it first.** Greetings, signatures, and "cc" lists can include names, phone numbers, or links back to your identity. Strip the note down before the AI ever sees it — see Step 2.
- **Trusting the AI to make the decision for you.** A table is a great mirror, but it cannot choose for you. If the AI's "Pros and Cons" feels off, ignore it and re-read your human notes from Step 4.
- **Forgetting the things no spreadsheet can measure.** Vacation days and salary are easy to compare; team vibe, manager style, commute, and growth path are not. If those rows are missing from your final table, the comparison is incomplete.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** the same habit — stripping personal info before pasting it into any chatbot — protects you whether you are comparing jobs, asking about medical symptoms, or sharing a tricky email you want help rewriting.
- **For your work or business:** if you ever help someone else compare offers (a partner, a friend, a mentee), walk them through the scrub-the-note-first step. It is the single most useful privacy habit to teach.
- **If you are just getting started with AI:** pick one task you already do by hand — comparing offers, drafting an email, summarizing a long article — and try it once with a free assistant. The skill is repetition, not genius.

## Try it now

Open your notes app, find one offer letter or email, and rewrite its facts into a fresh note with names and address removed. That single act is the whole habit — and it takes under two minutes.
